metas.name: Searching for Sugar Man
metas.description:
Captures fame existing in full, in a place the famous person never knew about. Detroit singer Rodriguez, a flop at home in the 1970s and rumoured dead, was bigger than Elvis in apartheid South Africa. The most joyful film in its batch.

Two South Africans set out to discover what happened to their unlikely musical hero, the mysterious 1970s rock n roller, Rodriguez.

metas.name: Anvil! The Story of Anvil
metas.description:
Captures artistic persistence with no payoff in sight. Toronto's own Anvil: fifty-something metal pioneers who nearly made it in 1982, now delivering school lunches and playing to five people in Prague, still completely serious about the band.

Since 1978, Anvil has become one of heavy metal's most influential yet commercially unsuccessful acts. In 2006, after a fledging European tour Anvil sets out to record their thirteenth album and continue to follow their dreams.

metas.name: Dont Look Back
metas.description:
Captures celebrity as combat sport, at the moment it was invented. Pennebaker inside Dylan's 1965 England tour: the cue-card sequence, Dylan dismantling journalists in hotel rooms, a persona manufactured in front of the lens.

Documentary covering Bob Dylan's 1965 tour of England, which includes appearances by Joan Baez and Donovan.

metas.name: Won't You Be My Neighbor?
metas.description:
Captures gentleness deployed as a discipline, not a temperament. Fred Rogers turns out to have been exactly as radical as he appeared: using children's television to insist, slowly and on purpose, that every child is lovable as they are.

An exploration of the life, lessons, and legacy of iconic children's television host Fred Rogers.

metas.name: Roadrunner: A Film About Anthony Bourdain
metas.description:
Captures charisma as both the gift and the mechanism of self-destruction. Anthony Bourdain's rise and suicide, told by the friends and crew who travelled with him and remain angry and bewildered in roughly equal measure.

A documentary about Anthony Bourdain and his career as a chef, writer and host, revered and renowned for his authentic approach to food, culture and travel.

metas.name: Diego Maradona
metas.description:
Captures fame as a hostage situation where the hostage keeps scoring goals. Kapadia builds Maradona's Naples years entirely from archive: adored as a god, pulled into the Camorra's orbit, collapsing under a worship no person could survive.

Constructed from over 500 hours of never-before-seen footage, this documentary centers on the career of celebrated football player Diego Maradona, who played for S.S.C. Napoli in the 1980s.

metas.name: Tim's Vermeer
metas.description:
Captures obsession as method: an engineering argument settled by actually doing the thing. Inventor Tim Jenison, who can't paint, spends years testing his theory that Vermeer used optical devices — by building the device and painting a Vermeer with it.

Inventor Tim Jenison seeks to understand the painting techniques used by Dutch Master Johannes Vermeer.

metas.name: Tower
metas.description:
Captures how people inside an event remember it — partial, sensory, nothing like the news summary. The 1966 UT Austin sniper massacre retold in rotoscoped animation from survivors' memories, switching to real footage only at the end.

Animation, testimony, and archival footage combine to relate the events of August 1, 1966 when a gunman opened fire from the University of Texas clock tower, killing 16 people.

metas.name: Sherman's March
metas.description:
Captures the personal documentary being invented out of failure. McElwee sets out to film Sherman's Civil War campaign, gets dumped before shooting starts, and the film becomes his disastrous search for love among old flames, narrated in a deadpan spiral.

Documentary filmmaker Ross McElwee sets out to make a movie about Union General Sherman's March to the Sea towards the end of the American Civil War, but keeps getting sidetracked by his own love life.

metas.name: Tarnation
metas.description:
Captures self-documentation as survival strategy. Caouette assembles his life from family photos, answering-machine tapes and home video — a mother destroyed by shock treatments and lithium, a childhood spent performing for cameras — edited on iMovie for a few hundred dollars.

Filmmaker Jonathan Caouette's documentary on growing up with his schizophrenic mother -- a mixture of snapshots, Super-8 film, answering machine messages, video diaries, early short films, and more - culled from nineteen years of ...

metas.name: Ex Libris: The New York Public Library
metas.description:
Captures a civic institution actually functioning as the thing it claims to be, which turns out to be quietly riveting. Wiseman, three hours, no narration: board meetings, story time, job-search classes, a branch deciding its budget at the New York Public Library.

A look within the walls of the New York Public Library.

metas.name: Primary
metas.description:
Captures the moment politics and television fused, visible as it happens. The film that invented American cinéma vérité: newly portable sync-sound cameras follow Kennedy and Humphrey through the 1960 Wisconsin primary, into rooms no camera had entered before.

Cinéma vérité feature that follows presidential hopefuls John F. Kennedy and Hubert H. Humphrey during the 1960 Wisconsin primary.

metas.name: Best Boy
metas.description:
Captures love expressed as letting go, at the lowest possible volume. Philly, a developmentally disabled man in his fifties whose elderly parents have done everything for him, is gently taught to live more independently — because they won't always be there.

In this documentary, the director follows the day-to-day activities of his intellectually disabled, middle-aged cousin Philly over a three-year period.

metas.name: The Cruise
metas.description:
Captures a mind turning a minimum-wage job into a total worldview. Timothy 'Speed' Levitch, a New York double-decker tour guide, treats the job as performance philosophy, riffing on grid plans, pigeons and mortality to busloads of tourists.

Timothy "Speed" Levitch, an eccentric New York City tour bus guide, takes tourists around the island of Manhattan and shares an archive of beautifully distorted information about the city.

metas.name: A Spring for the Thirsty
metas.description:
Captures a parable filmed in a desert: an old well-keeper, visited by memory and strangers, photographed by Yuri Ilyenko — the cinematographer of Shadows — in stark images the Soviet authorities shelved for over twenty years.

A parable centering on an old man who lives a secluded life in the desert, alone with only his memories and photographs. His wellspring, once a source of joy and hope for thirsty passersby, is now rarely used. No longer able to find comfort in his memories, he turns all his photographs to face the walls.

metas.name: The White Bird Marked with Black
metas.description:
Captures folk culture being torn by history. In the same Hutsul Carpathians as Shadows, four brothers in a village band end up on opposite sides of every border the war years drag across their valley, in images just as saturated.

A family struggles to survive in an area that was claimed as part of Rumania, Poland and Ukraine, all within a short span of time. When World War II comes, various family members choose different masters; some even choose to work for the Soviets. War, struggle, marriages, births, deaths--all these events punctuate the story of this large family.

metas.name: Stone Cross
metas.description:
Captures farewell as a whole way of life ending. A Ukrainian peasant spends his last night before emigrating to Canada saying goodbye, and carves himself a stone cross — the austere black-and-white twin of Shadows, from the same national school.

In 1890s Western Ukraine, Ivan Didukh, a proud and ripe Galician farmer, has decided to abandon his ancestral home to emigrate to Canada in search of a better life. His final hours are clouded by both internal and communal discord as his village convenes to ceremonially mark his departure. The celebrations that echo those of a funeral, forecast the imminent death of a man estranged from his motherland, and of an antiquated way of life on the cusp of obsoletion.

metas.name: Andrei Rublev
metas.description:
Captures an artist trying to make images of faith in a world of mud and violence. Medieval Russia through its greatest icon painter: raids, pagan festivals, and a boy casting a bell he may not know how to cast.

The life, times and afflictions of the fifteenth-century Russian iconographer St. Andrei Rublev.

metas.name: Pirosmani
metas.description:
Captures a film learning to see the way its subject painted. Georgian folk painter Niko Pirosmani's life built from his own canvases — taverns, feasts, animals, a man painting signs for food and dying unrecognised.

A biography of the Georgian primitive artist Nikoloz Pirosmanishvili (1862–1918), better known as Pirosmani, who died of starvation and sold his paintings to bars and restaurants for food and drink. The film experiments with color control techniques based on the painter’s style.

metas.name: The Legend of the Suram Fortress
metas.description:
Captures a filmmaker resuming exactly where the state interrupted him. Parajanov's return after prison and exile: a Georgian folk tale of a boy who must be immured in a fortress wall to make it stand, in full tableau style.

A film version of a well-known Georgian folk-tale. A young boy has to be immured into the walls of a fortress in order to stop it from crumbling to pieces.

metas.name: Ashik Kerib
metas.description:
Captures the tableau style at its most playful and weightless. Parajanov's last film, from Lermontov: a wandering minstrel must earn a fortune in a thousand days to marry, crossing Azerbaijani landscapes in living-embroidery compositions. Dedicated to Tarkovsky.

A talented but poor minstrel is forced to wander throughout the world because of impossibility to be with his true love - a rich merchant's daughter.

metas.name: Marketa Lazarová
metas.description:
Captures a whole civilisation changing gods. Medieval Bohemia in deep winter — pagan and Christian clans, wolf packs, kidnapped nuns, mud and chanting — with Shadows' savage lyricism stretched to epic scale. Frequently called the greatest Czech film.

A grim portrayal of the shift from Paganism to Christianity in medieval central Europe - as a young virgin promised to God is kidnapped and raped by a marauder who her religious father seeks to kill in return.

metas.name: Valerie and Her Week of Wonders
metas.description:
Captures puberty as a village fairy tale. A thirteen-year-old's coming-of-age rendered as folk-horror dream logic — vampire grandmothers, lecherous priests, possibly magic earrings — where every adult is a monster of one kind or another.

Surreal dream-like tale that combines several themes into one fantastical world.

metas.name: The Saragossa Manuscript
metas.description:
Captures storytelling itself as a folk labyrinth. A Napoleonic officer finds a manuscript and falls into tales within tales within tales — gypsies, kabbalists, ghosts, duels — for three hours in Wojciech Has's nested Polish epic.

Upon finding a book that relates his grandfather's story, an officer ventures through Spain meeting a wide array of characters, most of whom have a story of their own to tell.

metas.name: The Round-Up
metas.description:
Captures power as folk dance. On an endless white plain, authorities process prisoners from a peasant uprising through rituals of selection and betrayal, in Jancsó's choreographed long takes — nobody's psychology is explained, and the rituals are the point.

In Hungary, the national movement led by Kossuth has been crushed and the Austrian hegemony re-established, but partisans carry on with violent actions. In order to root out the guerilla, the army rounds up suspects and jails them...

metas.name: Häxan
metas.description:
Captures a lecture dissolving into delirium. Christensen's silent Swedish study of witchcraft keeps abandoning its own lecture format for re-enactments — sabbaths, torture chambers, possessed nuns — and from 1922 remains wilder than most folk horror made since.

Fictionalized documentary showing the evolution of witchcraft, from its pagan roots to its confusion with hysteria in Eastern Europe.

metas.name: I Even Met Happy Gypsies
metas.description:
Captures a community filmed from inside its own music and fatalism. A Romani feather trader in the mud flats of Vojvodina, folk songs everywhere, makes a series of choices each slightly worse than the last.

Tensions arise in a Gypsy community when a local feather seller falls in love with a much younger girl.

metas.name: Time of the Gypsies
metas.description:
Captures folk storytelling surviving, barely, inside modern crime. A Romani teenager with telekinetic powers is lured into a smuggling life in Italy, half narrated by Goran Bregović's score — Petrović's world taken into magical realism.

In this luminous tale set in the area around Sarajevo and in Italy, Perhan, an engaging young Romany (gypsy) with telekinetic powers, is seduced by the quick-cash world of petty crime, which threatens to destroy him and those he l...

metas.name: The Wicker Man
metas.description:
Captures paganism not as horror but as joy. A devout Christian policeman arrives on a Scottish island where the harvest failed and the old religion quietly resumed — and the islanders keep bursting into song, which is what makes the ending land.

A puritan police sergeant arrives in a Scottish island village in search of a missing girl, who the pagan locals claim never existed.

metas.name: Kwaidan
metas.description:
Captures folklore as pure painted atmosphere. Kobayashi adapts Lafcadio Hearn's ghost tales on vast studio sets — a snow spirit, a blind biwa player performing for the dead — the closest Japanese equivalent to Parajanov's tableau method.

A collection of four Japanese folk tales with supernatural themes.

metas.name: The Ballad of Narayama
metas.description:
Captures a folk custom at full earthiness. Imamura's mountain village carries its old people up the peak to die at seventy, filmed with his usual gusto for sex, cruelty and teeming nature — ritual without a trace of reverence.

In a poor 19th century rural Japanese village, everyone who reaches the age of 70 has to climb a nearby mountain to die. An elderly woman is reaching close to her cut-off age during her last days with her family.

metas.name: Gabbeh
metas.description:
Captures storytelling embedded in a folk object. A nomad tribe's woven carpet unfolds as it is washed in a river: the girl in the pattern tells her own story of forbidden love, in colours as saturated as Parajanov's Carpathians.

When an old couple washes their gabbeh - a type of Persian rug - a young woman magically appears and tells them her life story.

metas.name: Uncle Boonmee Who Can Recall His Past Lives
metas.description:
Captures an animist world where the supernatural needs no emphasis. A dying man in the Thai jungle is visited at dinner by his wife's ghost and his son returned as a monkey spirit, and everyone accepts this with total calm.

Dying of kidney disease, a man spends his last, somber days with family, including the ghost of his wife and a forest spirit who used to be his son, on a rural northern Thailand farm.

metas.name: Ten Canoes
metas.description:
Captures oral tradition's actual structure. In Arnhem Land, an elder tells a young man a cautionary ancestral tale inside which another tale is told, while they hunt goose eggs in the swamp — stories nested for a practical moral purpose, with jokes.

In Australia's Northern Territory, a man tells us a story of his people and his land. It's about an older man, Minygululu, who has three wives and realizes that his younger brother Dayindi may try to steal away the youngest wife.

metas.name: Pather Panchali
metas.description:
Captures lyricism at ground level. Ray's Bengal village childhood — Apu and his sister Durga, the monsoon arriving like a miracle — where poverty is filmed as a complete sensory world rather than a condition to be pitied.

Impoverished priest Harihar Ray, dreaming of a better life for himself and his family, leaves his rural Bengal village in search of work.

metas.name: Walkabout
metas.description:
Captures two cosmologies meeting in a landscape older than both. Two white children lost in the Australian outback are found by an Aboriginal boy on his walkabout; Eden and catastrophe share every frame.

Two city-bred siblings are stranded in the Australian Outback, where they learn to survive with the aid of an Aboriginal boy on his "walkabout": a ritual separation from his tribe.

metas.name: Aguirre, the Wrath of God
metas.description:
Captures conquest as a fever that keeps marching after its purpose has rotted. Herzog takes a conquistador expedition down the Amazon until the jungle, the raft and Klaus Kinski's face are all dissolving at the same rate.

In the 16th century, the ruthless and insane Don Lope de Aguirre leads a Spanish expedition in search of El Dorado.

metas.name: Days of Heaven
metas.description:
Captures labour, land and sky at a scale that makes human betrayal look like weather passing through it. Malick's wheat-harvest tragedy, shot almost entirely at magic hour and narrated by a child who only half understands the adults around her.

A hot-tempered farm laborer convinces the woman he loves to marry their rich but dying boss so that they can have a claim to his fortune.

metas.name: The Holy Mountain
metas.description:
Captures meaning stacked in images until it overloads. Jodorowsky's alchemical procession — a Christ figure and seven archetypes played by industrialists and generals — assembles some of the densest tableaux ever put on film, grotesque and deliberate.

In a corrupt, greed-fueled world, a powerful alchemist leads a messianic character and seven materialistic figures to the Holy Mountain, where they hope to achieve enlightenment.

metas.name: Amarcord
metas.description:
Captures a community remembering itself, every ritual half affection and half mockery. Fellini rebuilds his hometown of Rimini as permanent carnival: fascist rallies, family dinners, a peacock in the snow, a whole town rowing out to greet an ocean liner.

A series of comedic and nostalgic vignettes set in a 1930s Italian coastal town.

metas.name: Medea
metas.description:
Captures two cosmologies colliding. Pasolini casts Maria Callas, who barely sings a note, as the barbarian priestess Jason brings home to a rational, modern Corinth with no room for her gods — the archaic ritual world filmed in Cappadocia's stone landscapes.

After his quest to retrieve the fabled Golden Fleece, Jason returns to Greece with powerful sorceress Medea. However, when the king banishes her, it's only human that Medea plots her furious revenge. Can they escape her wrath?

metas.name: The Leopard
metas.description:
Captures pageantry as an instrument for measuring decay. Visconti's Sicilian prince watches his class dissolve during Italian unification, and the film saves its greatest set piece for a 45-minute ball where the old world dances beautifully with the one replacing it.

The Prince of Salina, a noble aristocrat of impeccable integrity, tries to preserve his family and class amid the tumultuous social upheavals of 1860s Sicily.

metas.name: Caravaggio
metas.description:
Captures a film thinking in paintings the way The Colour of Pomegranates does, but grubbier, queerer, and made for almost no money. Jarman stages the painter's life as living versions of his canvases, with calculators and motorbikes left sitting in the 1600s.

A retelling of the life of the celebrated 17th-century painter through his brilliant, nearly blasphemous paintings and his flirtations with the underworld.

metas.name: Prospero's Books
metas.description:
Captures maximalism as a system. Greenaway adapts The Tempest by layering handwriting, water, calligraphy and early digital compositing over John Gielgud voicing nearly every role — an image-world so dense it becomes a library you wander rather than a plot you follow.

The magician Prospero attempts to stop his daughter's affair with an enemy.

metas.name: The Fall
metas.description:
Captures storytelling as barter. Tarsem spent years shooting a suicidal stuntman's improvised fairy tale to a little girl in a 1920s hospital, across two dozen countries with no green screen; he needs her help, and she keeps changing the story by listening.

In 1920s Los Angeles, a bedridden patient in a hospital captivates a young girl with a fantastic tale of heroes, myths, and villains on a desert island.

metas.name: The Company of Wolves
metas.description:
Captures the folk tale's actual content — appetite, danger, metamorphosis — that the children's versions politely remove. Jordan and Angela Carter nest werewolf tales inside a sleeping girl's dream, all fog, forests and practical-effect transformations.

A teenage girl in a country manor falls asleep while reading a magazine, and has a disturbing dream involving wolves prowling the woods below her bedroom window.

metas.name: The Piano
metas.description:
Captures desire conducted entirely through objects, landscape and music. Campion's mute Scottish bride arrives in colonial New Zealand, and her piano, left on the beach by her husband, becomes the currency of a wordless negotiation in bush and mud that feel mythic.

In the mid-19th century a mute woman is sent to New Zealand along with her young daughter and prized piano for an arranged marriage to a farmer, but is soon lusted after by a farm worker.

metas.name: Raise the Red Lantern
metas.description:
Captures ritual as an instrument of control. Zhang Yimou confines a 1920s household drama to one courtyard compound, where the master's nightly choice of wife is announced by red lanterns and foot massages — rules never fully explained, which is how the women live them.

A young woman becomes the fourth concubine of a wealthy man and soon realizes there's fierce competition for his attention and the associated privileges.

metas.name: Yellow Earth
metas.description:
Captures a folk culture so total it becomes the cinematography. A Communist soldier arrives in a loess-plateau village in 1939 to collect folk songs for the army, and finds a girl whose singing is the only free thing in her life.

A communist soldier is sent to a remote region of China in order to collect folk songs. Staying with a peasant family (a widower with two small children), he discovers a community whose way of life is completely alien to him, but he gradually wins their trust.

metas.name: A Touch of Zen
metas.description:
Captures combat choreographed as calligraphy, then dropped entirely for transcendence. King Hu's wuxia epic follows a scholar drawn into a fugitive's fight against the imperial secret police, ascending through a bamboo-forest duel toward something close to enlightenment.

A lady fugitive on the run from corrupt government officials is joined in her endeavors by an unambitious painter and skilled Buddhist monks.

metas.name: The Cloud-Capped Star
metas.description:
Captures a woman being consumed by the goddess-provider role her culture assigned her. Ghatak's Calcutta family survives entirely on daughter Neeta's earnings and takes and takes, while the soundtrack whips and distorts under the melodrama — myth as the load-bearing structure.

A selfless young woman (Supriya Choudhury) sacrifices her own happiness for her unappreciative family.

metas.name: Moolaadé
metas.description:
Captures folk tradition argued with from inside folk tradition, in blazing colour. Sembène's Senegalese village has to renegotiate itself when one woman shelters girls fleeing the purification ritual, invoking the protective spell of the title against husbands, elders and merchants.

When a woman shelters a group of girls from suffering female genital mutilation, she starts a conflict that tears her village apart.

metas.name: Black God, White Devil
metas.description:
Captures a peasant world where religion and violence are the only available languages. Rocha's Brazilian sertão — a hired killer, a self-proclaimed saint gathering followers, a blind bandit-prophet — is filmed like a folk ballad being sung at gunpoint, in glare and dust.

After killing his employer when he tries to cheat him out of his payment, a man becomes an outlaw and starts following a self-proclaimed saint.

metas.name: Zama
metas.description:
Captures empire as a man rotting in a landscape that was never his and barely notices him. Martel strands a Spanish colonial officer in a Paraguayan backwater, waiting years for a transfer that never comes, while insects, water and distant animals become the real film.

Don Diego de Zama is a Spanish officer of the seventeenth century settled in Asunción, who awaits his transfer to Buenos Aires.

metas.name: The Travelling Players
metas.description:
Captures a nation's history carried by the people paid to keep entertaining it. Angelopoulos follows a folk theatre troupe performing the same pastoral play across Greece from 1939 to 1952, and in vast single takes, occupation, civil war and executions slide past mid-scene.

Greece, 1939-1952: Fascist, Nazi, and Communist conflict, as seen through the eyes of a family of travelling provincial players.

metas.name: Dry Summer
metas.description:
Captures a folk world running on a single resource, and how fast custom turns to feud when it runs short. Erksan's Anatolian village tears itself apart when one farmer dams the spring his neighbours' fields depend on.

A farmer has a violent dispute with his fellow villagers by claiming ownership of the water that comes out of his land. He is as sexually frustrated as greedy.

metas.name: Calendar
metas.description:
Captures diaspora as a loop of beautiful images you can't live inside. Egoyan sends a Canadian photographer to Armenia to shoot twelve ancient churches for a calendar, his marriage failing in the car between sites — then the ritual repeats, reframed, back in Toronto.

A woman stays in Armenia after her photographer husband completes his assignment and returns home to Canada.

metas.name: Hard to Be a God
metas.description:
Captures maximalism as immersion rather than beauty. German's scientist observes a filthy, violent medieval world on another planet, forbidden to intervene, across three hours of black-and-white mud, smoke and faces pressing into the lens — total world-building with every trace of lyricism drowned.

In the distant future, a space traveler from Earth breaks a special law and interferes with the history of another, Medieval-like planet.

metas.name: The Tribe
metas.description:
Captures a complete social world you must learn to read bodily or not at all. At a Ukrainian boarding school for deaf students, a student crime network runs everything — performed entirely in sign language, with no subtitles and no translation.

A deaf boy joins a boarding school for similar children. Confronted by the violent and criminal antics of some of the other boys and girls, he struggles to conform and join the 'tribe'.

metas.name: Tale of Tales
metas.description:
Captures folk memory itself — images from childhood, war and lullaby sharing one continuous dream. Norstein's 29-minute animation drifts through layers of cut-out, glass and mist: a little wolf, a minotaur, tango dancers, soldiers leaving for the front.

Distant, well-worn memories of childhood are inhabited by a little gray wolf. Through astonishing imagery, the memory of all of Russia is depicted.

metas.name: Alice
metas.description:
Captures the folk tale as a child's-eye inventory of a household's dangerous things. Švankmajer's Alice moves through a Wonderland of taxidermy, bones and jam jars of pins, stop-motion objects that genuinely threaten her — Carroll's dream rebuilt from junk drawers.

A surrealistic revision of Alice in Wonderland.

metas.name: The Tree of Wooden Clogs
metas.description:
Captures the folk world at the opposite end of the temperament scale from Parajanov — patient, plain, and quietly overwhelming. Olmi films Lombardy peasants playing their grandparents' generation: four families, one farm, a whole year of seasons, labour and ritual.

Peasant life in a feudal farm in rural Italy at the end of the 19th century.

metas.name: Shadows of Forgotten Ancestors
metas.description:
Captures a folk tale carried by image and ritual rather than plot. Parajanov's Hutsul lovers Ivan and Marichka move through Carpathian weddings, funerals and seasons in whirling camera work, saturated colour and embroidered imagery. The film Filip confirmed watching and enjoying.

A timeless Carpathian story - the young Ivan falls in love with the daughter of his father's killer among the Hutsul people of Ukraine.
